questions.knowledge_point: Determining the One-Dimensional Image of a Linear Transformation in the Cartesian Plane
questions.problem:
Let
$T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]$
be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Then $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $T$ has proportional rows, and yet $T$ is not the zero matrix. 

Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=1$ and $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line that passes through the origin.

Moreover, the line must pass through the origin $(0,0)$ and the points $(1,3)$ and $(2,6),$ which are defined by the columns of the matrix $T.$ 

Computing the slope $m$ of this line, we get

$$
m=\frac{6-3}{2-1}=3.
$$

 

Therefore, $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto the line $y=3x.$

questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $T$ has proportional rows, and yet $T$ is not the zero matrix. 

Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=1$ and $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line that passes through the origin.

Moreover, the line must pass through the origin $(0,0)$ and the points $(-4,2)$ and $(2,-1),$ which are defined by the columns of the matrix $T.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying True Statements Regarding Linear Transformations in the Cartesian Plane
questions.problem:
Consider a linear transformation $T$ that maps ${R}^{2}$ to the origin. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\text{nullity}(T)=0$
- $\text{Ker}(T)={0}$
- $\text{rank}(T)=0$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when the image of a linear transformation $T$ in ${R}^{2}$ with the standard matrix $T$ is the zero-subspace ${0},$ then

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=0
$$

and, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T) & =2-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =2-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is false. We have that

$$
\text{nullity}(T)=2.
$$

- Statement II is false. The condition $\text{nullity}(T)=2$ in ${R}^{2}$ is equivalent to 

$$
\text{Ker}(T)={R}^{2}.
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, we have

$$
\text{rank}(T)=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying True Statements Regarding Linear Transformations in the Cartesian Plane
questions.problem:
Consider a linear transformation $T$ that maps ${R}^{2}$ onto the line $y=-2x.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $⟨-1,2⟩\in \text{Im}(T)$
- $\text{Ker}(T)={R}^{2}$
- $\text{nullity}(T)=0$, where $T$ is the standard matrix of $T$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that when the image of a linear transformation $T$ in ${R}^{2}$ with the standard matrix $T$ is a one-dimensional line, then

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=1,
$$

and, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T) & =2-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =2-1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the point $(-1,2)$ satisfies the equation of the line $y=-2x$ since $2=-2\cdot (-1).$ Hence, 

$$
⟨-1,2⟩\in \text{Im}(T).
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $\text{nullity}(T)=1,$ we get 

$$
\text{Ker}(T)\ne {R}^{2}.
$$

- Statement III is false. We have that 

$$
\text{nullity}(T)=1.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying True Statements Regarding Linear Transformations in the Cartesian Plane
questions.problem:
Consider a linear transformation $T$ that maps ${R}^{2}$ onto ${R}^{2}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $⟨1,1⟩\in \text{Im}(T)$
- $\text{Ker}(T)\ne {0}$
- $\text{nullity}(T)=0$, where $T$ is the standard matrix of $T$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a linear transformation $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto  ${R}^{2}$ if and only if 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=2
$$

and, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T) & =2-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =2-2 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, The condition $\text{rank}(T)=2$ in ${R}^{2}$ is equivalent to 

$$
\text{Im}(T)={R}^{2}.
$$

Hence, $T$ is surjective and so  $⟨1,1⟩\in \text{Im}(T).$

- Statement II is false. The condition $\text{nullity}(T)=0$ in ${R}^{2}$ is equivalent to 

$$
\text{Ker}(T)={0}.
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, we have that 

$$
\text{nullity}(T)=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
